recipes.name: All-Day Apple Butter
ingredients_raw: 5.5 pounds apples - peeled, cored and finely chopped

steps.text: Place apples in a slow cooker. Combine sugar, cinnamon, cloves, and salt together in a medium bowl; pour over apples and mix well.
Cover and cook on High for 1 hour.
Reduce heat to Low and cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture is thick and dark brown, 9 to 11 hours.
Uncover and continue cooking on Low for 1 hour. Whisk to make smooth, if desired.
Spoon mixture into sterile containers, cover; refrigerate or freeze.

raw_recipe.headline: All-Day Apple Butter
raw_recipe.description: This apple butter recipe cooks apples, sugar, and spices in the slow cooker until smooth, buttery, and full of rich flavor for a sweet taste of fall.

video.description: Let your slow cooker make this irresistible apple butter for you.
video.name: How to Make All-Day Apple Butter

review.reviewBody: This is definately a keeper. I used Golden Delicious apples, and put them through the food processor VERY FINE before I started. This way I didn't have any lumps, and didn't have to mess with hot butter later on. We like really spicy apple butter, so I increased the spices a little, but then added 1/2 tsp. ground allspice. I also only used about 2 cups sugar. Put it on before I went to bed, and then in the morning took the lid off and let it cook another few hours where I could watch it to get the consistancy I wanted. (I checked it by putting a spoonful on a saucer and looking after it got cold to see if there was any water separation.)

This is excellent. I used Gala apples and just 2 cups of sugar and found that to be enough sweetness. During the last hour I took the lid off the crockpot so the apple butter can thicken and I used my immersion blender to break up chunks of apple. It gave the apple butter a great smooth texture. I made three batches of this apple butter last year to give as gifts and I am back to this recipe to make it again this year.

This is a great recipe. I had no idea it was so easy to make apple butter. I had a lot of apples on my trees this year. I love this recipe but I did try a couple of variations. I used just over one cup of sugar. I liked it better a bit tart. I cut the apples into chunks instead of small pieces and then put them in the crock-pot on high; I would add more apples as they cooked down so my crock-pot was full. I let them cook, covered on high overnight. After they got soft I removed the lid and let them cook down while I was at work (about 6 hours). Since they were in chunks the thinner liquid made them not stick and burn like a thick liquid would have. They reduced down to between 2/3 to ½ of a crock-pot. When I got home I took my immersion blender and blended them up and the thickness was just about perfect. I tried the saucer test for doneness. I put them in my sterilized jars and put them in a hot water bath for 30 minutes. Now I have my Christmas presents ready to go, cheap, fabulous and homemade! It just doesn’t get any easier. I made this with pears also and it was good but not quite as good as the apple. I also tried one batch with unpeeled apples and there is a huge difference. Take the time to peel the apples. Thanks for this recipe. I ended up making about five batches and each batch made about 9 half pints.

Excellent base recipe! Definitely a keeper! Used Gala and Pink Lady apples- 3lbs each. Chopped up apples into bite size pieces- added 1 3/4 cups light brown sugar, 2 Tsp ground cloves, 1TBSP cinnamon, 2 tsp apple pie spice. Mixed and using a food processor chopped into smaller bits- this had to be done in small batches. Placed back in crock pot, covered and cooked on low for 10 hrs- checking to mash down larger bits. Removed and put in processor again and processed til a smooth consistency. Returned to the crock pot and cooked on high for 1hr mixing occasionally. Consistency thickens as it cools. Canned in 1/2 pint jars- yield 4-6 jars.

My favorite apple butter recipe! I have found this fills around 9 to 11 half pint jars. Kind of depends on how juicy your apples are or how much moisture cooks out. Or maybe its because I weigh my apples after I have peeled and cored them.

My favorite variation: Substitute half of the weight of the apples with fresh cranberries! Run the cranberries through your food processor using the shredding blade first. This will make an amazing cranberry apple butter!

Tip: prepare and get it started in the slow cooker in the evening, or about 12 hours before you will be awake the next morning. Then it can cook all night unattended and its ready in the morning to put in jars and process/can. 

I have also used only 3- 3.5 cups of the sugar and it still tastes great. I much prefer to taste the apples and spices rather than a bunch of sugary sweetness.

Absolutely incredible. 
I followed some of the suggestions of other reviewers and did one batch with 1.5 cups white sugar + .5 cup brown sugar (i.e. the sugar amount gets halved). Ended up throwing it all, a few cups at a time, into my blender after 9 hours, then uncovered as is in the recipe for 1-2hrs. Came out stellar!
Next batch I did 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup blown sugar (i.e. 3/4 sugar amount). Left overnight untouched 10 hrs, then in the morning I blended it all a few cups at a time, let it sit heating uncovered for a few hrs and voilà! Perfection. This batch came out more caramelized, and personally I feel is more fit for pancakes and waffles due to sweetness.

If I'd known making apple butter was THIS EASY with a slow cooker, I'd have been making it years ago. Fresh apples are so plentiful here in northern CA. It's such a great way to use apples that aren't ideal for eating raw due to texture, size or high tartness.

Will make again and again and again!!!

I read the reviews and added 1/4tsp allspice. I also started it at around 12pm left it on high for an hour then turned it down to low, that night at around 10pm I set it to warm. The next morning I put it back on low for about 4 hours then took off the lid and set it on high for about 3 hours. I also used my immersion blender to blend it which worked wonders. Oh, I chopped the apples up in my processor before putting them in the crockpot. I checked to see if it was done by placing a wooden spoon upright in the center of the crockpot till it stood up straight on its own. I then filled canning jars and bathed them for a half hour. It turned out great. The long wait is well worth it. I'll definitely use this recipe again.

I doubled this recipe but kept the sugar right at 3 cups since I used 5 pounds of gala apples and 5 pounds of red delicious. The apples are already sweet. Cooked it in my slow cooker for 22 hours making just over 6 pints and processed in the canner for 10 minutes. Absolutely delicious and unbelievably easy.

I made this per the recipe and found it to be VERY sweet. Next time I will start with 2 cups of sugar and add more at the end, if needed. Also, I used an immersion blender after the apples cooked down to make it a smooth, and even consistancy. Overall, it's a good recipe.

I used a combination of Macintosh and golden delicious apples I did not peel the apples. I ran the apple butter through my food mill in the end to make it smooth and creamy. I only used 2 cups of sugar. Added a half teaspoon of allspice to the spice mixture. It’s an easy recipe. Your slow cooker does all the work. I put the apple butter into sterilized, hot pint jars, sealed them, and put them in a hot water bath for 15 minutes. Add a pretty ribbon. and they’re ready for giftgiving.

Fantastic!! So good!! Came here to say Thank you to the person who shared that they used the Pressure Cooker on high for 7 min with quick release after 10 min. 5 hrs in slow cooker on high. I then canned with water bath method for 20 min.
Everyone that tries it wants the recipe!

I have been making this recipe for years. I use a mix of different apples on mine. I do not add all this sugar tho. I start with half and then add to my liking. I do no peel the apples either. That is my fav part. Such a simple recipe and so easy. Mine get all canned so we can enjoy it through out the yr.

Very flavorful and easy. I didnt peel the apples, not wanting to lose the nutrients. Diced the apples small. used allspice, cinnamon, and cloves. However, I did reduce the sugar by 25%. When cooking complete, I used my blender to make a really smooth butter.
Way way too sweet!
So easy, and truly delicious! I added a dash of nutmeg and that really made the dish.
I added nutmeg and allspice. Had my house smelling divine all day.
Super easy recipe - I did not peel the apples but I chopped in small bits and used my immersion blender to create a smooth texture - delicious!

EDIT Sept 17, 2023 I only used 1/2c sugar this batch and it was amazing. Yum! I can't believe how much over 5lbs of apples can cook down. I only used 2 c of sugar and it is plenty sweet. It's great that this takes all day to cook because it makes the house smell great.
Made this last year and my MIL said it was exactly like her mommy used to make when she was a little girl. Thank you for sharing this recipe. It’s a keeper!
